explanation: RAII is a fundamental C++ programming idiom that ties resource management to an object's lifetime.  Resources (like dynamically allocated memory, files, network connections, mutexes, etc.) are acquired in the object's constructor and released in its destructor. This guarantees that resources are always properly cleaned up, even in the presence of exceptions or premature function exits.  This eliminates memory leaks, resource exhaustion, and other common errors associated with manual resource management.
